Turn a public article into an evidence-linked summary.

Choose a public article and paste a short permitted excerpt. Ask for a summary with facts and uncertainties separated. Ask for a table of claims and exact supporting excerpts. Check each claim against the original.
Produce a one-page briefing with three verified claims and one open question.
Do not paste confidential customer data; a confident answer is not evidence.
Review a long technical document with a structured rubric.
Select a public document. Give the model a checklist for assumptions, dependencies and limitations. Request page or section identifiers. Independently inspect every cited section.
Create a review matrix with finding, evidence and suggested correction.
Confirm applicable document upload and retention policies; never assume unlimited context.
Build a multimodal analysis exercise using a public chart.
Choose a chart with known values. Ask for axis labels and three data points. Compare the transcription with the source. Ask for a short interpretation that separates observation from inference.
Report exact-value errors and two limitations of the analysis.
Small labels and cropped legends may cause misinterpretation.
Research a technology question using primary sources.
Ask a narrow question with a date range. Open the cited links rather than relying on the summary. Compare an official document with independent evidence. Record what remains uncertain.
Write a sourced research note with links and publication dates.
A citation can be real but fail to support a claim.
Create a learning notebook from permitted course material.
Add public documentation or documents you have rights to use. Ask a question whose answer is present. Ask an unanswerable question. Check the citations and produce a revision guide.
Create five study questions and verify their answers in the sources.
Do not upload materials that violate organizational data policies.
Use an AI editor to improve a small application safely.
Create a disposable Git branch and a tiny test suite. Ask for a plan before editing. Review the diff line by line. Run the tests and compare the result with the original behavior.
Submit a reviewed patch and a passing regression test.
Review permissions, commands and new dependencies before execution.
Write and test a Python utility with a coding assistant.
Write a function contract with examples. Request an implementation and edge-case tests. Run tests locally. Review the generated code for licensing, correctness and secret handling.
Implement a CSV validation utility with documented failures.
Generated code can be insecure even if it compiles.
Work on a small repository through a controlled coding task.
Use a test repository without credentials. Specify acceptance tests and permitted files. Inspect the proposed changes before committing. Run the existing tests and a new regression case.
Prepare a small reviewed pull request with a clear test result.
Avoid granting unrestricted production access to coding agents.
Investigate and fix a reproducible bug in an isolated repository.
Make a clean branch and reproduce the error. Ask for a hypothesis tied to source files. Request the minimal fix and test. Inspect the diff, command history and test output.
Document the root cause, patch and reproduction steps.
Review tool permissions and do not expose internal logs or tokens.
Explore visual composition with controlled prompt variations.
Use your own permitted reference. Specify subject, lighting, composition and aspect ratio. Change one variable per generation. Compare results and record the settings.
Build a three-image concept board with a short critique.
Generated images are not documentary evidence; respect likeness and licensing rights.
Plan and review an AI-assisted editorial image.
Use a licensed input or a text-only prompt. Generate several compositions. Check artifacts, text and brand references. Review export terms before publishing.
Produce an image brief with a provenance note.
Do not imply generated photographs depict actual events.
Create a short visual sequence from a permitted reference.
Write a shot list and define motion. Generate a brief clip. Check continuity of subjects and lighting. Revise one shot rather than regenerating the whole sequence.
Prepare a short sequence with a visible synthetic-media label.
Obtain permission for recognizable people and copyrighted inputs.
Choose a model by reading model cards and evaluating a small task.
Identify a narrow task. Compare two model cards for license, intended use and requirements. Test both on ten representative examples. Record accuracy and resource use.
Write a model-selection report with a fallback baseline.
Open weights do not automatically imply unrestricted commercial use.
Experiment with a local language model.
Read the installation instructions for your operating system. Select a model that fits available memory. Run a public-text prompt. Measure latency and review network activity and model license.
Compare local and hosted options using identical test prompts.
Local inference is not proof that the entire application is private.
Train and evaluate a small neural classifier.
Follow the official tensor and dataset tutorials. Split a public teaching dataset before training. Train a small model and monitor validation loss. Inspect errors by class.
Produce a reproducible notebook with loss curves and held-out accuracy.
Avoid test leakage and record environment versions.
Build an introductory image classification pipeline.
Use a public educational dataset. Apply preprocessing consistently. Train a baseline model and validate on held-out samples. Compare predictions on unfamiliar examples.
Document a training run and its failure cases.
High validation accuracy does not guarantee production generalization.
Start with a small public text corpus. Index passages with source IDs. Retrieve candidates for each question. Generate a response with citation IDs and an abstention rule.
Measure retrieval recall on ten known questions.
Treat retrieved documents as untrusted content and enforce permissions outside the model.
Compare chunking strategies for a documentation assistant.
Choose a public manual. Split by headings and compare fixed-token chunks. Store source metadata. Evaluate whether each strategy retrieves the passage needed to answer a question.
Report recall at five and citation-support quality.
Remove revoked documents from indexes and caches.
Understand a read-only MCP tool integration.
Read the protocol architecture. Inspect a local demo server's tool definitions. Validate arguments in the host application. Test denied actions and timeouts using synthetic data.
Document tool schemas, authorization boundaries and failure handling.
MCP is an integration protocol, not a complete authorization policy.
Design an approval-gated workflow using a mock API.
Start with a manual trigger. Transform a synthetic record. Validate required fields. Add an approval step and route failures to an error branch.
Demonstrate a successful run and a rejected malformed record.
Store credentials in the approved secret mechanism, never in workflow text.
Experiment with vector search and metadata filtering.
Create a local teaching collection. Insert embeddings and document identifiers. Query with a similar passage. Apply a metadata filter and compare exact and approximate search.
Report retrieval quality, latency and filtered results.
Apply authorization during retrieval; a result filter in the UI is too late.
Track two model experiments and compare them fairly.
Create an experiment with a fixed dataset split. Log parameters, metrics and environment versions. Run a second candidate. Register a version only after reviewing held-out performance.
Produce an experiment comparison and rollback plan.
Avoid logging raw secrets or personal data in artifacts.
Draw the trust boundaries. Identify prompt injection, excessive privileges and data exposure. Add deterministic authorization and output validation. Test with synthetic malicious instructions.
Create a risk register and five reproducible security tests.
Test only authorized systems; do not equate prompt defenses with access control.
Design a support agent using approved learning environments.

Use a Trailhead module or authorized sandbox. Define the topic, permitted actions and escalation criteria. Test a normal request and a denied action. Review the trace and correct ambiguous instructions.
Document an agent scenario, action permissions and test outcomes.
Do not expose production customer data or grant broad write access.
Design a small server-side summarization integration.

Read current authentication and model documentation. Keep credentials in server-side environment variables. Validate input size and output schema. Handle timeout, quota and invalid responses explicitly.
Write a small integration with mocked failure tests and a cost budget.
Never embed API credentials in GitHub Pages JavaScript.
